overall_summary: Analysis of the deduplicated performance metrics highlights that extreme cosmic phenomena and 'What If' hypothetical space scenarios are drastically outperforming standard biology, psychology, and general fact formats. Videos focusing on bizarre planetary conditions (e.g., liquid diamond planets, burning ice planets, and supersonic ruby rain) posted within the last 7 to 30 days show the highest velocity in views-per-day and engagement (likes-per-view up to ~3.7%). Conversely, older psychology and standard animal facts have stagnated.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (IYuce8vaU3Y) and 'What If You Fell Into the Planet of Burning Ice?' (8KEl0_pJ_68) generated over 1,000 views and exceptionally high likes (up to 38) within a short window compared to older static facts.
winning_patterns.action: Double down on high-stakes hypothetical space immersion scenarios featuring extreme environments.

winning_patterns.evidence: 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (A9Qa-RmuOr0) and 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (v1rrcZLdp4U) accrued ~1,000 views and strong viewer retention indicators.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more short-form deep dives into scientifically verified yet physically baffling exoplanets and celestial mechanics.

weak_patterns.evidence: 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (2fqaGqfsR4A, r43-7nSn8SQ) and song-stuck psychological tricks yielded minimal traction (5-10 views, 0 likes) over extended monitoring periods.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone human psychology and memory tricks in favor of high-visual-potential space and physics topics.

weak_patterns.evidence: Basic trivia like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' received decent initial views in past weeks but show low relative engagement on recent reruns compared to exotic space topics.
weak_patterns.action: Rest standard animal facts unless paired with a high-stakes cinematic survival or extreme evolutionary mystery angle.
